footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $26.0M attributable to noncontrolling interests, $376M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 4.4% to $28.5B in 2025. Net interest income rose 2.2% to $16.6B and noninterest income rose 7.6% to $11.9B; noninterest expense fell 2.0%, and the provision for credit losses was $2.2B, versus $2.2B.
Net income to common rose 21.7% to $7.2B, or $4.62 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 59.0% versus 62.9%. U.S. Bancorp returned $3.7B through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 21.7% to $7.2B.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
sources: U.S. Bancorp Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
